name: Bael'dun Digsite
summary: Dwarven prospectors cut into the western hills of Mulgore at Bael'dun Digsite. Their search for ancient Titan relics has brought them into conflict with the tauren, who see the digging as an insult to the Earth Mother.

sections.title: Intrusion in the Hills
sections.body: Dwarven prospectors dig into the mountain slopes of western Mulgore. Their camp marks the southernmost reach of the Explorers' League expedition based at Bael Modan in the southern Barrens. The dwarves came with picks, shovels, and blasting powder, seeking ancient Titan relics buried beneath the plains. They paid no heed to borders or to the spiritual traditions of the newly settled tribes.

sections.title: Defending the Earth Mother
sections.body: The Bloodhoof tribe sees the digging as an assault on the Earth Mother. Baine Bloodhoof first urged caution and warned the dwarves to leave, but they refused to abandon their trenches. With diplomacy failed, the tauren resolved to break the expedition's tools and drive out the miners before their digging cuts deeper into Mulgore's sacred earth.

faq.q: Why are dwarves digging in Mulgore?
faq.answer: The prospectors belong to the dwarven expedition based at Bael Modan in the southern Barrens. The Explorers' League seeks ancient artifacts and Titan heritage, and the dwarves chose this outpost where their instruments pointed to relics, disregarding tauren sovereignty.

faq.q: How does the Bloodhoof tribe respond to the digsite?
faq.answer: The tauren see the digsite as a wound against the Earth Mother. After the dwarves refused early warnings to leave peacefully, Baine Bloodhoof and the village leaders sent warriors to destroy the miners' tools and drive them from Mulgore.

faq.q: What is the connection between Bael'dun and Bael Modan?
aliases: where do these dwarves come from
faq.answer: Bael'dun is an outpost of the fortress and main excavation at Bael Modan, just across the mountain ridge in the southern Barrens.

faq.q: Why didn't the tauren simply negotiate with the expedition?
faq.answer: Baine Bloodhoof first tried diplomacy and warned the expedition leaders. The dwarves treated Mulgore as unclaimed wilderness and ignored tauren spiritual concerns, leaving the tribe to use force.

angles.text: As a tauren, you see Bael'dun's scars on Mulgore's western hills as an insult to the Earth Mother. The ancestral soil must be defended from foreign desecration.
As an Alliance member, you may understand the miners' thirst for historical discovery. Their digging has reached deep into Horde territory and brought them into violent conflict with the locals.
